name: Oaxaca
shortPitch: A highland food-and-culture weekend built around markets, Zapotec history, and mountain day trips.
highlights: Eat tlayudas, memelas, mole, and smoky market snacks at 20 de Noviembre
Walk Monte Albán's hilltop plazas and tombs
Spend a day at Hierve el Agua or with weavers in Teotitlán del Valle

weather.note: Dry-season sunshine makes walking easy; mornings and evenings are cool at elevation.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; the exact Nov. 11–15 itinerary can require a connection, especially from DC and SF.

travel.description: Fly into OAX; compact city center and most food-and-history stops are walkable once there.

caveat: A short trip can be squeezed by awkward flight times, so check the door-to-door itinerary as closely as the fare.

name: Cartagena
shortPitch: A hot, walkable walled city where Caribbean history, Getsemaní murals, and Colombian cooking fill three days.
highlights: Trace ramparts, plazas, and the Castillo San Felipe fortress
Eat arepas de huevo, ceviche, and Caribbean seafood in Getsemaní
Take a neighborhood-and-history walk through the Walled City

weather.note: Very warm and humid; November is drier than fall but brief showers still happen.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; East Coast routings are generally kinder than SF.

travel.description: Fly into CTG; the historic core is compact, but heat changes the pace of daytime sightseeing.

caveat: It is strongest as a city-and-history trip only if the group is happy to skip the usual beach and nightlife emphasis.

sources.title: UNESCO: Port, Fortresses and Group of Monuments

name: Antigua
shortPitch: A colonial mountain town that can pair cobblestone wandering and coffee with a real volcano outing.
highlights: Explore ruined churches, plazas, and rooftop views beneath Agua Volcano
Visit a coffee farm or taste Guatemalan chocolate and local cooking
Hike Pacaya or commit to the overnight Acatenango volcano trek

weather.note: The dry season is beginning: mild days, cool nights, and clearer volcano views.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; add the road transfer from Guatemala City airport.

travel.description: Fly GUA, then allow roughly 60–90 minutes by road to Antigua depending on traffic.

caveat: Acatenango is spectacular but strenuous and consumes a large share of a three-day trip.

name: Lima
shortPitch: A serious food city with pre-Columbian ruins, Pacific neighborhoods, and enough distinct cuisines for a focused long weekend.
highlights: Compare ceviche, Nikkei, and chifa cooking across Barranco and Miraflores
Visit Huaca Pucllana, an adobe pyramid in the city
Walk the historic center, museums, and Pacific cliffs

weather.note: Mild and often gray rather than sunny; rain is uncommon.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; the long flight makes every departure hour matter.

travel.description: Fly LIM; airport-to-neighborhood traffic can be slow, but the city supports a dense itinerary once checked in.

caveat: The food is a major draw, but it is less naturally outdoorsy than several candidates.

name: Medellín
shortPitch: A green, high-energy mountain city with cable cars, neighborhood history, and a huge granite monolith day trip.
highlights: Ride the Metrocable and explore the city’s hillside transformation
Visit Comuna 13 murals, Museo de Antioquia, and central markets
Day-trip to Guatapé and climb El Peñol's 700-plus stairs

weather.note: Springlike temperatures year-round, but showers are possible in November.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; SF usually has the least convenient routing.

travel.description: Fly MDE; plan around the airport-to-city transfer and a long-but-worthwhile Guatapé day.

caveat: Its nightlife reputation can hide the cultural and outdoor itinerary; the group would need to choose the latter deliberately.

name: Quito
shortPitch: A high-altitude colonial capital with enormous Andean scenery close enough for a city-and-volcano weekend.
highlights: Walk the UNESCO-listed historic center and its churches
Ride the TelefériQo toward high páramo trails
Choose a Cotopaxi, cloud-forest, or equator-line day trip

weather.note: Cool at 9,000 feet with changeable showers and clear mountain windows.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; altitude and variable weather add practical planning weight.

travel.description: Fly UIO; allow time to acclimate before a hard hike or high-elevation day trip.

caveat: Altitude is not theoretical—hard activity on day one can be a bad bet for some travelers.

name: El Salvador
shortPitch: A compact, active country that combines volcanoes, crater lakes, coffee country, and a very strong pupusa itinerary.
highlights: Hike Santa Ana Volcano above Lake Coatepeque
Eat pupusas in Olocuilta and explore San Salvador’s history
Drive Ruta de las Flores for coffee farms, small towns, and waterfalls

weather.note: Dry season is starting, with warm days and clearer volcano views.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; good value depends on accepting a road-trip itinerary.

travel.description: Fly SAL; a rental car or private driver unlocks the best volcano and coffee-country days.

caveat: The best version is less polished and involves more moving around than a single-city weekend.

name: Guadalajara
shortPitch: A large, elegant Mexican city for markets, murals, mariachi, lucha libre, and Jalisco food beyond its drinking stereotypes.
highlights: See Orozco’s murals at Hospicio Cabañas
Eat birria, tortas ahogadas, and market breakfasts
Browse Tlaquepaque workshops or catch lucha libre

weather.note: Dry, sunny afternoons and cool evenings suit long walking days.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; this is comparatively kind to the SF traveler.

travel.description: Fly GDL; the city has airport access, neighborhoods, and major sights without requiring a side trip.

caveat: If tequila tours are not the point, the itinerary must lean on the city’s art, food, and public-life strengths.

name: Bogotá
shortPitch: A cool, sprawling Andean capital for gold, street art, mountain views, and a salt-cathedral day trip.
highlights: See the Gold Museum and colonial La Candelaria
Ride or hike Monserrate for city-and-Andes views
Go underground at Zipaquirá Salt Cathedral

weather.note: Cool, often cloudy, and periodically rainy—bring layers and a rain shell.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; East Coast value is usually stronger than SF.

travel.description: Fly BOG; the city is large, so cluster each day geographically and account for traffic.

caveat: The climate and scale are a real contrast with a sunny, compact long-weekend getaway.

name: Monterrey
shortPitch: A northern Mexican city in a dramatic limestone bowl, built for serious hiking and carne asada between urban stops.
highlights: Hike Chipinque or La Huasteca beneath the Sierra Madre
Walk Parque Fundidora and visit MARCO
Eat cabrito, carne asada, and northern Mexican staples

weather.note: Usually dry and comfortable for hiking, with cooler nights.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; one of the more convenient western-origin options.

travel.description: Fly MTY; a car makes the trailheads and canyon landscapes much easier to reach.

caveat: It has outstanding mountains but a less immediately distinctive historic core than the central Mexican contenders.

name: Puebla + Cholula
shortPitch: A practical Mexico City gateway with mole, talavera, colonial streets, and a giant pyramid under volcano views.
highlights: Eat mole poblano, cemitas, and sweets on a market-and-bakery crawl
Climb Cholula’s pyramid and see the church on top
Explore Puebla’s tiled center, tunnels, museums, and lucha libre

weather.note: Dry, sunny, and mild; evenings are noticeably cool at elevation.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; fly MEX, then add a bus or private transfer to Puebla.

travel.description: Use Mexico City’s deep flight network, then plan roughly two hours of ground transfer each way.

caveat: The extra airport-to-Puebla transfer is the tradeoff for much better flight-market flexibility.

name: Granada + León
shortPitch: Colonial cities plus volcanic Nicaragua: lake, markets, murals, and a legitimately strange sandboarding day.
highlights: Walk Granada’s colorful center and Lake Nicaragua waterfront
See León’s cathedral, murals, and revolutionary history
Board down Cerro Negro or hike Masaya and Mombacho volcanoes

weather.note: Dry season begins; mornings are clear and lowland afternoons are hot.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; transfers are a material part of the cost in time.

travel.description: Fly MGA; Granada and León are in different directions, so the itinerary needs deliberate routing.

caveat: The variety is excellent, but moving between cities and volcanoes can burn valuable hours.

name: Guanajuato
shortPitch: A colorful hillside maze of theaters, mines, tunnels, plazas, and high overlooks—built for wandering.
highlights: Navigate underground roads and climb to the Pípila overlook
Tour a historic silver mine and the unusual Mummy Museum
Eat market snacks and linger in plazas, callejones, and music-filled evenings

weather.note: Dry, pleasant walking weather with crisp highland nights.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; BJX is a smaller airport than MEX.

travel.description: Fly BJX, then transfer about 30 minutes to the historic center; hills and stairs are part of the experience.

caveat: Flight connectivity is thinner than Mexico City or Guadalajara, and the terrain is not accessibility-light.

name: Copán Ruinas
shortPitch: A focused Maya archaeology expedition: carved stelae, a sculpture museum, macaws, and coffee-country hills.
highlights: Explore Copán’s stelae, ball court, tunnels, and Hieroglyphic Stairway
Spend time in the site’s Sculpture Museum
Pair ruins with Macaw Mountain and a coffee-country outing

weather.note: Warm days and cooler evenings, with rain tapering off.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; the long ground transfer is the larger constraint.

travel.description: Fly into San Pedro Sula, then plan roughly four hours by road each way to Copán Ruinas.

caveat: It is extraordinary once there, but a three-day trip spends a meaningful fraction in transit.

name: Detroit
shortPitch: An industrial-America curveball of Motown, design, factory history, museums, sports, and exceptional Middle Eastern food.
highlights: Spend a full day at the Henry Ford Museum and Greenfield Village
See Motown and the Detroit Institute of Arts
Eat through Dearborn’s Yemeni and Lebanese restaurants or Eastern Market

weather.note: Cold and variable; this is primarily an indoor culture-and-food weekend.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; simple domestic access is a major advantage.

travel.description: Fly DTW; most anchors are reachable with a short drive or rideshare.

caveat: It is a great weekend, but not the same ‘we went somewhere wild’ feeling as several international or park options.

name: Québec City
shortPitch: Old stone walls, French-Canadian food, and a compact North American city that feels unusually European.
highlights: Walk Old Québec, the Citadelle, and fortified city walls
Eat Québecois classics and modern French-Canadian cooking
See Montmorency Falls and the Musée de la civilisation

weather.note: Mid-November can be chilly, wet, or snowy with short daylight.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; weather and seasonal schedules deserve a final check.

travel.description: Fly YQB; the old city is walkable, but winter layers are mandatory planning gear.

caveat: This timing may deliver gray shoulder-season weather rather than storybook snow.

sources.title: UNESCO: Historic District of Old Québec

name: Banff
shortPitch: Early-winter Canadian Rockies for glacier lakes, canyon walks, gondola views, hot springs, and weather-dependent snow.
highlights: See Lake Louise and drive the Icefields Parkway if conditions allow
Walk Johnston Canyon or take the Banff Gondola
Soak in hot springs after a cold mountain day

weather.note: Early winter: cold, snowy, and condition-dependent; daylight is short.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; add Calgary-to-Banff ground transport and winter contingency.

travel.description: Fly YYC, then travel about 90 minutes to Banff; a car or shuttle and weather-aware itinerary are essential.

caveat: This is real winter travel, not a casual fall hike; road and trail conditions set the agenda.

name: Cleveland
shortPitch: A low-friction industrial-city sleeper: art, rock history, old markets, sports, and Cuyahoga Valley trails.
highlights: Visit the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame and Cleveland Museum of Art
Eat at West Side Market and old-school neighborhood spots
Hike, bike, or ride the scenic railroad in Cuyahoga Valley National Park

weather.note: Cold and potentially rainy; outdoor plans are workable in layers.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; domestic logistics leave more usable weekend time.

travel.description: Fly CLE; the city and national park are a short drive apart.

caveat: It is remarkably easy, but lacks the geographic drama of the top outdoor candidates.

name: Sedona
shortPitch: A red-rock hiking trip with enough trail variety, stargazing, and a comfortable town base to fill every daylight hour.
highlights: Hike Cathedral Rock, Bell Rock, or Devil’s Bridge
Walk West Fork of Oak Creek Canyon
Drive red-rock scenery and stargaze in the dark-sky landscape

weather.note: Crisp, sunny hiking days with chilly desert nights.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; fly PHX, then drive about two hours.

travel.description: Use Phoenix as the airport, rent a car, and make trail timing the center of the weekend.

caveat: This is intentionally outdoor-heavy; the town is pleasant, but not a culture-and-food city in the same way as Oaxaca or Lima.

name: Moab
shortPitch: A concentrated desert-geology weekend: two national parks, giant arches, canyon overlooks, and very little filler.
highlights: Hike among Delicate Arch and other formations in Arches
See Canyonlands overlooks and Dead Horse Point
Choose Corona Arch, Fisher Towers, or a petroglyph outing

weather.note: Cool, dry days and freezing nights; occasional snow is possible.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; gateway and car-rental timing matter.

travel.description: Fly to Grand Junction or Salt Lake City and drive; the landscapes are spread across a wide area.

caveat: The scenery is huge, but access is awkward and November cold shortens the flexible outdoor window.

name: Chattanooga
shortPitch: A compact Appalachian city where river-gorge scenery, Civil War history, and easy food stops all fit in one weekend.
highlights: Hike Lookout Mountain, Signal Mountain, or Tennessee River Gorge
Visit Chickamauga and Chattanooga Civil War sites
Eat downtown and explore the riverfront or Tennessee Aquarium

weather.note: Usually cool and pleasant for hiking, though rain is possible.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; a connection may be needed from some origins.

travel.description: Fly CHA or drive from Atlanta; the core is compact and trailheads are close.

caveat: Very good at many things, but the scenery is more Appalachian than once-in-a-lifetime Utah or Rockies spectacle.

name: Zion / Springdale
shortPitch: An elite national-park hiking base with canyon walls, big trail payoffs, and easier flights than its remoteness suggests.
highlights: Hike the Watchman or canyon routes from Springdale
Attempt Narrows sections only if weather and water conditions cooperate
Explore Kolob Canyons or Observation Point-area terrain

weather.note: Cool, often clear hiking weather; water hikes depend on forecast and flow.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; Las Vegas fares are easy, but the drive is not optional.

travel.description: Fly LAS and drive roughly 2.5 hours to Springdale each way; park shuttles handle much of the core.

caveat: The Vegas drive plus short November days demands an early, focused itinerary.

name: El Paso → Guadalupe Mountains + Carlsbad Caverns
shortPitch: A deliberately weird desert road trip: El Paso food, Texas’s highest peak, and a vast underground national park.
highlights: Eat El Paso borderland Mexican food before driving east
Hike Guadalupe Peak or McKittrick Canyon
Descend Carlsbad Caverns’ Natural Entrance and see the Big Room

weather.note: Mild, dry surface days and cold nights; Guadalupe winds can be strong. Cavern interiors stay near 56°F.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; a rental car and long desert mileage are part of the deal.

travel.description: Fly ELP, then road-trip several hours east through the Chihuahuan Desert to the parks.

caveat: The road time and limited city content are not bugs; they are the premise, and the group has to want that.

name: Palm Springs → Joshua Tree + San Jacinto + Salton Sea
shortPitch: A surreal Southern California triangle: desert boulders, a high-mountain tramway, midcentury Palm Springs, and the strange Salton Sea.
highlights: Hike and scramble among Joshua Tree’s granite and yucca
Ride the tram to San Jacinto’s 8,500-foot trails
See Salton Sea oddness, then eat and walk Palm Springs architecture

weather.note: Warm desert days and cool evenings; San Jacinto is dramatically colder at elevation.

airfare.qualifier: Typical round-trip planning estimates; East Coast PSP routing is manageable rather than effortless.

travel.description: Fly PSP, rent a car, and use Palm Springs as a base for three very different landscapes.

caveat: It works best for a group excited by landscape variety and weirdness, not one expecting a single cohesive historic city.
